text:
sana: quick follow-up from the pagination/retries RFC thread. we still lack a tight cross-language contract for how resume cursors, client prefetch, and transport selection should behave together. my gut proposal: (a) clients expose language-native iteration (generators / async iter / channels), (b) resume state is an opaque token managed by the transport, and (c) callers pass an explicit `retry_hint` so the runtime/transport can pick retry/backoff/dup-detection strategy. thoughts? :thinking:

ryan: agree with opaque token + retry_hint. ergonomics idea: iterator yields Page objects; Page.resume_token is opaque. transports accept small handshake headers: `X-Resume-Token`, `X-Call-Shape` (paged|stream|unary) and `X-Retry-Hint`. TS example: 

```
for await (const page of client.listThings({ retryHint: 'idempotent' })) {
  // page.items
}
```

marta: main concern is prefetch semantics. if a client prefetches N pages up front and one of those prefetched requests fails with non-idempotent semantics, the visible behavior differs from a strictly-lazy iteration. propose two client modes: `strict` (no cross-page prefetch when retry_hint != idempotent) and `optimistic` (allow prefetch but surface failures normally). default should be `strict` to avoid surprising duplicates or lost side effects.

jeremy: +1. let's standardize `retry_hint` values to: `idempotent`, `at_most_once`, and `at_least_once`. runtime will map these to: retry/backoff strategy + duplicate-detection TTL when available. default for list/list-like ops should be `idempotent`.

sana: language defaults: python generators = lazy (prefetch=0) by default; go channels = prefetch=0 by default; ts/JS may choose prefetch=1 for better UX but must document mismatch. also expose explicit `prefetch` opt-in so clients can pick. we'll put a parity note in the docs.

ryan: transport-side handshake sketch: send `X-Resume-Token: <opaque>` (or omit when none), `X-Call-Shape: paged|stream|unary`, and `X-Retry-Hint: idempotent|at_most_once|at_least_once`. router can choose best route or fallback. keeps the client/transport API minimal.

marta: example Go usage for explicit control:

```
pages := client.ListThings(ctx, &ListOptions{RetryHint: "idempotent", Prefetch: 0})
for p := range pages {
  // handle p.Items
}
```

jeremy: one more tricky area: stream <-> paged fallback. if a client requests `paged` semantics but the chosen route only supports a streaming RPC, the transport should either: (1) provide a thin adapter that groups stream messages into page boundaries (best effort), or (2) fail with an explicit error and let the client opt into a fallback policy. we must avoid silent, surprising semantic changes.

sana: implementation + docs action items: 1) one-page contract doc describing header names + resume token lifetime/semantics, 2) language snippets and a prefetch/backoff defaults table (python, ts, go), 3) add headers to transport shim and implement router mapping. volunteers? @ryan @marta

ryan: i'll take the transport header + router sketch PR.

marta: i'll write the python + go examples and notes on prefetch safety defaults.

jeremy: i'll map `retry_hint` -> runtime retry/backoff policy and add the duplicate-detection TTL guidance.

sdk-bot: [RFC tracker] follow-up created: https://redwood.internal/rfcs/0.12.3#followups

sana: great. i'll file concise action items in the RFC thread and link the PRs. thanks all! :rocket:
